\mxunit{enrichment-inequalities-notes}{Inequalities and equality cases}
\mxsubtitle{High school · optimisation and olympiads \textperiodcentered{} Lesson and method \textperiodcentered{} 11}

\begin{prerequisites}
Squares, factorisation and square roots.
\end{prerequisites}

\begin{keypoint}[Ideas and method]
For every real $u$, $u^{2}\geq 0$, with equality exactly when $u=0$. Many inequalities reduce to this observation.

For $a,b\geq 0$, $(\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b})^{2}\geq 0$ gives $a+b\geq 2\sqrt{ab}$, the arithmetic--geometric mean inequality. Equality holds exactly when $a=b$.

Proving a bound is not enough to announce a maximum: an admissible equality case must attain it. Positivity and domain conditions are part of the argument.
\end{keypoint}

\begin{example}
If $a+b=10$ with $a,b\geq 0$, then $(a-b)^{2}\geq 0$ gives $100-4ab\geq 0$, so $ab\leq 25$. The pair $a=b=5$ attains 25, proving that it is the maximum.
\end{example}

\begin{activity}[Explore]
Plot $f(x)=x(10-x)$ for $0\leq x\leq 10$ and move the point. Then prove the maximum without relying on the picture.
\end{activity}
